## Outcome
Create the selected stack with pnpm workspaces for TypeScript apps, Flutter tooling for mobile, Prisma migrations, local Docker Compose, and synthetic demo data.

## Planning
- Draft ID: M03
- Phase: 1
- Area: Foundation
- Priority: P0
- Depends on: M01 (#1)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Web, Android, and API run using documented commands with validated environment examples.
- [ ] Database migrations and a repeatable synthetic seed are included; no production credentials or data are committed.
- [ ] CI builds apps and checks formatting, types, and critical domain tests.
- [ ] Pin compatible stable dependencies; CI runs Next.js/NestJS checks and Flutter analyze/test/build. Generate or validate TypeScript and Dart contracts from OpenAPI.

## Definition of done
- Acceptance criteria verified with relevant evidence.
- Critical transaction changes include failure, retry, and concurrency checks.
- UI follows the design system, including loading, empty, and failure states.
- Documentation describes supported behavior and limitations.

Status: Draft specification; implementation has not started.
## Implementation entry gate
M01 (#1) is complete; scaffolding can begin while #2 stays In QA. Establish separate `apps/web` (Next.js owner back office), `apps/mobile` (Flutter Android cashier), and `apps/api` (NestJS) boundaries, or document equivalent paths. Web must not expose a cashier/cart/checkout route. Both clients consume the versioned API; transactional rules remain server-owned.

- [ ] A clean clone can start the database/API/web and build the Android debug app with documented commands.
- [ ] CI validates the OpenAPI document and generates/compiles both TypeScript and Dart clients; document generation commands and prevent contract drift.
- [ ] Record toolchain versions, environment variables, migration/seed commands, and health checks. Use synthetic data only.

Completion of this ticket enables #4, #6/#7 and the hardware spike #15; it does not mark production business flows or visual approval complete.

content.body:
## Description
The #28 owner walkthrough found that the primary sidebar exposes only Menu, Stock, Sales, Reports, Printers and Settings (`apps/web/components/sidebar-nav.tsx:15`). Nine implemented routes are reachable only through secondary links: Promotions, Purchasing, Bookkeeping, Shifts, Attendance, Online ordering, Customers, Audit search and Permissions. A new owner has no reliable path to these modules.

Add grouped, role-aware primary navigation entries so every implemented module is discoverable without knowing a URL. Keep the existing secondary links working.

Source: #28 (friction F1).

## Positive Acceptance Criteria
- Primary navigation exposes Menu, Stock, Sales, Reports, Promotions, Purchasing, Bookkeeping, Shifts, Attendance, Online ordering, Customers, Printers, Audit search, Permissions and Settings, grouped sensibly.
- Every listed route is reachable in at most one click from any back-office page.
- An owner sees all implemented modules; a cashier sees only modules the API permits for that role.
- The active route is marked with `aria-current="page"` and the nav remains usable at 320 px without horizontal page overflow.
- Existing web format, typecheck, tests and shell checks still pass.

## Negative Acceptance Criteria
- Do not remove or rename existing routes, pages or deep links.
- Do not add product behaviour beyond navigation and role visibility.
- Do not change API endpoints, database schema or seed data.
- Do not show a cashier an owner-only module as an enabled primary destination.
- Do not create duplicate navigation entries for the same route.

## Planning
- Phase: 3
- Area: Back-office web UX
- Priority: P2
- Depends On: #28 (source discovery); related usability umbrella #29

content.body:
## Description
During the #28 walkthrough a cashier saw the Reports item in primary navigation. Opening it issued four `GET /v1/outlets/{outletId}/reports/daily` requests, each returning 403, and stayed in a loading state for roughly four seconds before showing `Only an owner can read sales reports for this outlet.` The API correctly enforces owner-only access (`apps/api/src/reports/reports.controller.ts:14`); the client hides no destination by role and uses the default query retry policy (`apps/web/components/reports-screen.tsx:116`).

Make the web navigation and the Reports screen role-aware, and bound the failed request instead of retrying an authorization error.

Source: #28 (friction F2).

## Positive Acceptance Criteria
- A cashier does not see Reports as an enabled primary navigation destination.
- A cashier opening `/reports` directly sees an explicit owner-only state without an unbounded retry loop; the failed request is attempted at most once and the error appears within one second on the staging VPS.
- The message names the action: reading sales reports requires an owner.
- An owner still sees the full report, CSV export and existing refresh behaviour.
- Web format, typecheck and tests pass, including a cashier-role render test.

## Negative Acceptance Criteria
- Do not weaken or remove the API owner-only guard on report reads or CSV export.
- Do not hide Reports or CSV export from an owner.
- Do not invent report values, fall back to another outlet or show partial data after 403.
- Do not change report calculations or date-range semantics.

## Planning
- Phase: 3
- Area: Back-office web UX
- Priority: P2
- Depends On: #28 (source discovery); related usability umbrella #29

content.body:
## Description
The #28 walkthrough created a printer through `POST /v1/outlets/{outletId}/printers` and confirmed it with `GET /v1/outlets/{outletId}/printers?deviceId=...`. The Printers page still showed `No printer registered` because the status card is hard-coded (`apps/web/components/printers-screen.tsx:136`) and the page never calls `listPrinters`. An owner cannot tell whether a printer is configured or which model/transport is registered.

Add an owner-visible, read-only printer configuration view. If the API cannot list outlet printers without a device ID, add an owner-authorized read path that returns only non-secret printer metadata.

Source: #28 (friction F3).

## Positive Acceptance Criteria
- When at least one printer config exists for the outlet, the Printers page lists its name, model, transport, paper width and encoding.
- When no printer config exists, the page shows an explicit empty state that does not claim a failed connection.
- Loading and error states are present and retryable.
- The page remains read-only and states that pairing, discovery and physical printing stay on the Android device.
- Web format, typecheck and tests pass, including a populated-printer render test.

## Negative Acceptance Criteria
- Do not expose connection secrets or credentials in the web response or UI.
- Do not claim that a listed printer is physically connected, online or tested.
- Do not add device discovery, pairing or print execution to the web app.
- Do not change the device-ownership rule for print jobs.
- Do not show another outlet's printer configuration.

## Planning
- Phase: 3
- Area: Back-office web UX / printing metadata
- Priority: P2
- Depends On: #28 (source discovery); related usability umbrella #29

content.body:
## Description
During the #28 walkthrough a cashier saw a History button on every stock card (`apps/web/components/stock-screen.tsx:879`). Clicking it called `GET /v1/outlets/{outletId}/stock/{stockItemId}/movements`, which is owner-only (`apps/api/src/stock/stock.controller.ts:43`), and returned 403. The displayed message was `This account is not allowed to change outlet settings.` (`apps/web/lib/api-errors.ts:12`), which describes a different action and a change rather than a read.

Remove the cashier dead-end and give stock read failures a stock-specific explanation. If read-only movement history for cashiers is desired later, scope it in a separate ticket with an explicit permission decision.

Source: #28 (friction F4).

## Positive Acceptance Criteria
- A cashier does not see an enabled History action that is guaranteed to return 403.
- A stock read failure shows a message about viewing stock history, not about changing outlet settings.
- An owner can still open movement history and see the append-only ledger.
- The stock screen still renders balances, filters and count/waste links for cashiers.
- Web format, typecheck and tests pass, including a cashier render test.

## Negative Acceptance Criteria
- Do not expand the API movement-history permission without a separate decision.
- Do not hide movement history from an owner.
- Do not change stock balances, movement records or count semantics.
- Do not replace the generic error helper in unrelated owner-only write screens in a way that changes their meaning.
- Do not add customer data to the screen.

## Planning
- Phase: 3
- Area: Back-office web UX / permissions
- Priority: P2
- Depends On: #28 (source discovery); related usability umbrella #29

content.body:
## Description
The #28 walkthrough used the Sales screen to locate a recorded receipt. The screen supports only outlet-local date inputs and loads 25 rows at a time (`apps/web/components/sales-screen.tsx:953`); the API list query has no reference filter. To investigate a support call an owner must widen the range and page through every sale. The sale reference is stable and already stored, so a server-side reference search is feasible.

Add a reference search to the Sales filter, scoped to the selected outlet and date range.

Source: #28 (friction F5).

## Positive Acceptance Criteria
- The Sales screen accepts a full or partial sale reference in a search field.
- Search is applied by the API, not by filtering only the first loaded page.
- Results respect the selected outlet, date range and caller role.
- Clearing the search restores the normal date-filtered list.
- No results, loading and error states are explicit.
- API and web format, typecheck, tests and OpenAPI checks pass.

## Negative Acceptance Criteria
- Do not add customer-name, phone or email search in this ticket.
- Do not expose sales from another outlet or business.
- Do not change receipt totals, reversal behaviour or sale state.
- Do not scan unbounded history; keep the date range required.
- Do not return customer PII in the list response.

## Planning
- Phase: 3
- Area: Back-office web UX / sales lookup
- Priority: P3
- Depends On: #28 (source discovery); related usability umbrella #29
